findings.statement: domain reading: older/heavier, frequent visitors (more so smokers) higher risk; high income relative to score lower risk
findings.evidence: plausible directions; no conflict with known domain knowledge; 'score' has no stated real-world meaning, so the income-score reading stays relative

age_bmi_hinge.why: A joint age-BMI threshold above which predicted risk climbs steeply, heavier people reaching it younger; the age-by-BMI probe confirms the switch-on points.

linear_age_bmi_score.why: The direction (risk up a little with age and BMI, down with score) is confirmed, but the part mainly sets the logit baseline and its variation adds almost no ranking (AUC 0.837 -> 0.834 at its mean), so there is no reading beyond a small slope.

visits_smoker_hinge.why: Risk rises above about 3-4 visits, and smoking lowers that threshold by about one visit and adds a constant once on, so smoking matters only for frequent visitors; probes and subgroup counts confirm it.

income_score_hinge.why: High income relative to score lowers predicted risk, with a higher score pushing the protective income threshold up; the income-by-score grid confirms it, though 'score' itself has no stated real-world meaning.
